Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

towards preposition

in the direction of

also toward

classical

Mart. 14.172.1: ad tē reptantī … lacertae
Liv. 1.4.6: ad puerīlem vāgītum cursum flexisse

ad (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

towards, to

In the direction of a thing, whether one gets there or not (see to).

Other words

  • versus (after its noun) — towards (a place)

    adverb placed after its noun: after ad or in + accusative, or after the accusative alone of a town’s name · classical · Sulp. in Cic. Fam. 4.5.4: ab Aegīnā Megaram versus nāvigārem; Cic. Lael. 96: in forum versus agere cum populō

    It marks the direction only: Megaram versus, towards Megara; in forum versus, facing the forum; ad Ōceanum versus, towards the Ocean (Caes.).

  • obviam — towards (someone coming), to meet

    adverb, with a dative and a verb of motion · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.5.1: quam longissimē poteris obviam nōbīs prōdeās

    Going towards someone who is coming: obviam īre, prōdīre, venīre, go out to meet.

Examples

  • ad tē reptantī, puer īnsidiōse, lacertae parce

    spare the lizard creeping towards you, sly boyMart. 14.172.1–2

  • lupam sitientem ex montibus quī circā sunt ad puerīlem vāgītum cursum flexisse

    that a thirsty she-wolf from the hills round about turned her steps towards the children’s cryingLiv. 1.4.6

  • ex Asiā rediēns cum ab Aegīnā Megaram versus nāvigārem

    on my way back from Asia, as I was sailing from Aegina towards MegaraSulp. in Cic. Fam. 4.5.4

  • quam longissimē poteris obviam nōbīs prōdeās

    come out to meet us as far along the road as you canCic. Fam. 14.5.1

  • Currēns itaque Esau obviam frātrī suō, amplexātus est eum

    so Esau ran to meet his brother and embraced himVulg. Gen. 33.4

See also to, behind, opposite.
